units.translation: and those who hold the whole mainland-born race
and a wailing together with shrieks held the sea
the shapely tombs of the land of Ilium hold them
before seeing this man holding a bed on the ground of a silver-walled coffin
and the highest gods and the heavily honored chthonic ones who hold the tombs
having held with a healing hand
but my son, having learned, held and soothed
so that the Atreidae could not hold back tears
and to hold back the guard of the fair-prowed mouth, a curse-laden voice for the house
to hold the ruinous part of the land
for the eye of one who thinks well accuses you
for the tongue of vain thoughts becomes a true accuser for men

said of Minerva, of one sitting, whose feet are covered by garments, as Wellauer pointed out. For palladia [statues of Pallas] were not only upright, but also seated, about which, among others, Porphyrius spoke in his notes on Homer Il. 6, 273. See what I said in Philologus in the year 1861 p. 344.
he places the foot upright or covered
faulty for ἐγκατιλλώψας [having looked askance at], which see.
to waste away, to make lean
to waste away, to make lean
Thus Robortellus for κατισχαίνουσα [wasting away], which is in M.
I did not think that I would be wasted away by such punishments
I know the assembly of the night stars
but my son, not knowing these things, accomplished them with youthful daring
I settled blind hopes in them
deprived of my fatherland, you settled me
who will one day settle Themiscyra
where H. L. Ahrensius has μέτοικος [resident alien], Scaliger κάτοικτος [pitiable]: if he restored correctly, it is said once as ἐποίκτιστος [much lamented] and ἔποικτος [lamented] 1221 1614.
why then do I, an inhabitant, lament thus?
whence Eum. 121 I restored ἄγαν ὑπνώσσεις καὶ κατοικτίζει πάθος [you sleep too much and pity the suffering], for κατοικτίζεις [you pity], which is in M.
the rent of the tunic will not pity the deed
why do you delay and pity in vain?
you sleep too much and pity the suffering
perfect middle κατόλωλα I have perished, in tmesis
for the youth has now all perished
Thus Meineke for κατολολυξάτω [let him cry aloud].
cry aloud, O you, for the victim to be stoned
The same words are joined by Io. Cinnamus p. 157 d.
and I sent scouts and spies of the army
I myself am a spy of the affairs
the spy of the army brings us some news, friends
Thus Canterus corrected what is in M κάτοπτρον [mirror] from the scholiast who explains it as τὸ κατόψιον [the visible].
the headland of the Saronic strait, visible
